# The problem: only stem (0,1)-(104,105) forms (as 0-105/1-104), others too weak.
# Spurious: 0-12, 1-11 (a 2bp helix between pos 0-1 and 11-12).
# We need all 5 stems to form. 2-bp GC helices are weak (~-1 each) but the alternative 0-12 fold competes.
# Strategy: use GC pairs (strongest) for all stems, and break the 0-12 spurious by making pos 11-12 NOT complementary to 0-1.
# Currently S3 (11,12)-(89,90). If 0-1 = GC and 11-12 = GC, then 0(G)-12(C)? No, 0 pairs with 12 means G-C (complementary). That's the spurious.
# To break: make 11-12 = CG (reverse) so 0(G)-12(G) not complementary, 1(C)-11(C) not complementary.
# But then S3 (11-12)-(89-90): 11=C pairs 90=? must be G; 12=G pairs 89=? must be C. So 89=C,90=G. That's fine.
# Let me set stems so adjacent same-strand runs don't self-complement.
t="((...((....((.....((.........((..............................))...............)).........)).......))....))...."
st=[];pairs={}
for i,c in enumerate(t):
    if c=="(": st.append(i)
    elif c==")": j=st.pop(); pairs[j]=i;pairs[i]=j
    else: pairs[i]=-1
seq=['A']*110
# S1 (0,1)-(104,105): GC
seq[0]='G';seq[1]='C';seq[104]='G';seq[105]='C'  # wait need complementarity: 0-105, 1-104. 0=G,105=C ok; 1=C,104=G ok
# Actually pairs: 0-105,1-104. So seq[0]comp seq[105]; seq[1]comp seq[104].
seq[0]='G';seq[105]='C'
seq[1]='C';seq[104]='G'
# S3 (11-12)-(89-90): pairs 11-90,12-89. Make 11=G,90=C; 12=C,89=G. Then 0(G)-12(C) is complementary! bad.
# Try 11=C,90=G;12=G,89=C. Then 0(G)-12(G) no; 1(C)-11(C) no. Good breaks spurious.
seq[11]='C';seq[90]='G'
seq[12]='G';seq[89]='C'
# S2 (5-6)-(98-99): pairs 5-99,6-98. GC: 5=G,99=C;6=C,98=G

seq[6]='C';seq[98]='G'
# S4 (18-19)-(78-79): pairs 18-79,19-78. GC: 18=G,79=C;19=C,78=G
seq[18]='G';seq[79]='C'
seq[19]='C';seq[78]='G'
# S5 (29-30)-(61-62): pairs 29-62,30-61. GC: 29=G,62=C;30=C,61=G
seq[29]='G';seq[62]='C'
seq[30]='C';seq[61]='G'

print(s)

# We'll randomize stem assignment but ensure strong (GC or CG only)

    fc=RNA.fold_compound(s)
    fc.sc_update_seqs()
    mfe,e=fc.mfe()
    return mfe,e

def random_stems():
    # assign each stem a 2-mer, ensure each strand-adjacent closing pair differs
    seq=['.']*110
    choices=['GC','CG','GG','CC']  # 2-mers; complement pairs
    for k,(i,j) in enumerate(sp):
        L=choices[random.randrange(len(choices))]
        # complement reverse for right side
        R=L[::-1].translate(str.maketrans('GCAU','CGUA'))
        seq[i]=L[0];seq[i+1]=L[1] if (i+1)==sp[k][0]+1 else L[1]
        # left 2 positions i and i+1 (consecutive in this stem)
    # Actually left strand of each stem is i, i+1 consecutive. Right strand is j-1, j consecutive (since pairs are i-i' and i+1-(i'-1))
    return seq

def build(stem_choices, loopseq):
    seq=['A']*110
    for (i,j),L in zip(sp, stem_choices):

        seq[j]=comp[L[0]]; seq[j-1]=comp[L[1]]
    for idx,pos in enumerate(loop_positions):
